instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups of rice until the water runs mostly clear. Add it to a medium saucepan with 2 1/4 cups of water, bring it to a boil, then cover and turn the heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave the lid on.
In a small bowl, mash the miso, the soft butter and the sugar with a fork until smooth. If the butter is cold, cut it into small pieces first.
Pat the salmon dry and cut it into 4 pieces. Spread the miso butter over the top of each piece.
Cut the cabbage into 2-inch pieces and the onion into thin wedges. Slice the carrots into thin coins. Trim the base off the enoki and pull the mushrooms apart. Slice the scallions.
Heat the oil in a large deep skillet with a lid over medium. Add the cabbage, onion and carrots. Cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until the cabbage wilts. Add the enoki and cook for 1 minute.
Spread the vegetables flat and set the salmon on top, miso side up. Pour the sake around the fish.
Cover right away and turn the heat to low. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily at the thickest part.
Take off the lid. If the vegetables look watery, turn the heat to high for 1 to 2 minutes to cook off the extra liquid.
Sprinkle the scallions and pepper over the top. Taste the vegetables. If they're flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve the salmon and vegetables with the pan juices and the rice.
method_notes: No Recipes is the lead (4.75 from 8 ratings, so a fallback): miso, butter and sugar spread on the salmon, then steamed over cabbage, onion, carrot and enoki with sake. JETRO-style and Shinagawa versions agree on salmon with cabbage, onion and mushrooms steamed under a lid. Shinagawa also adds potato, mirin and soy sauce to the sauce and browns the fish first; this version follows No Recipes and keeps the sauce to miso butter. The amounts are scaled up from 450 g of salmon for 4 to suit a main dish.
